function_question: How does nature find things in the dark?

opening.text: There was a boy called Ali who loved fixing things and helping his little sister, Sara.
Sara played with her toy robot, which beeps back whenever you clap. She never let it out of her sight.
The power went out, the torch battery was flat, and the robot was lost somewhere in the dark room. "I can't see anything!" Sara cried.

card.problem: A toy is lost in the dark
card.goal: Find hidden objects using only sound
card.rules: No light allowed, stay seated when blindfolded

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: Lights out!
chapters.line: Ali wonders: how do you find something when you can't see at all?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Ali needs a detective partner
chapters.line: Two sharp pairs of ears are better than one. Will you join Ali?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The night heroes
chapters.line: You and Ali meet heroes who hunt and fly in total darkness.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the echo

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: Training in the echo lab

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. The lights are out at Ali's house, and his little sister's toy robot is lost in the dark. Can you help him find it using only sound? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some detectives already have a spark of an idea for finding things without seeing them. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been finding things in the dark for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four night heroes!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which sound will help you hear the tray best? Stay seated with your blindfold on.
guide.sketch: Time to draw your Echo Finder kit, with arrows for the sound going out and coming back!
guide.build_and_test: Build your kit and play the blindfold game. How many of the 5 hidden spots can you find?
guide.retry_tip: Detectives never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing, like a sharper click or bigger ear cones, and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, whenever the lights go out, Ali and Sara play the echo game. Sara's robot has never been lost for long!

quick_check.question: A bat's click flies to a moth 2 metres away and bounces back to the bat. How far did the sound travel altogether?
quick_check.right: Right! The sound goes 2 metres there and 2 metres back, so 4 metres. That's why a far-away echo takes longer to come back.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Remember, the sound has to go there AND come back.

clue_cards.name: Bat
clue_cards.trick: It shouts high clicks and listens for the echoes.
clue_cards.does: It can catch a tiny moth in total darkness.

clue_cards.name: Dolphin
clue_cards.trick: It sends clicks out through the fatty bump on its forehead.
clue_cards.does: The echoes show it fish hiding in murky water.

clue_cards.name: Oilbird
clue_cards.trick: It makes clicks we can hear, deep inside dark caves.
clue_cards.does: The echoes stop it crashing into the cave walls.

clue_cards.name: Barn owl
clue_cards.trick: Its two ears sit at different heights on its head.
clue_cards.does: It hears which ear a sound reaches first, and pounces in the right spot.

match_groups.label: 📣 Sends a sound, hears the echo

predict.prompt: Quick echo or slow echo? Predict first!

items.label: Clapping right next to a wall
A bat clicking at a moth just in front of it

predict.explain: Sound travels about 340 metres every second. The farther away something is, the longer its echo takes to come back.

lab.title: The Echo or No Echo lab
lab.predict: Blindfolded, can you hear if a tray is 30 cm in front of your face? Which sound will work best?

tool.name: Nature Translator
tool.intro: The Nature Translator turns your problem into a question nature can answer. Today you'll learn the first 2 steps: F and Q.

parts.name: Function
parts.what: Say what your design must DO, using an action word.
parts.example: ☂️ An umbrella must keep rain off you.
parts.starter: My design must help Ali find…

parts.name: Nature question
parts.what: Turn that action into a question starting with 'How does nature…?'
parts.example: ☂️ How does nature keep rain off?

sketch_checklist: I drew the sound I send and the echo coming back.
I labelled my clicker and my ear cones.
I marked the 5 spots where the object could hide.

test.check_question: Ear check: when did you find the most spots?

reflection.question: Which nature trick helped you find things in the dark?
